title.narrative: Emergency WASH Response for drought-affected population in Baydhaba rural areas

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia has faced protracted insecurity and recurrent climate shocks, resulting in nearly 6 million people in need of humanitarian assistance in 2025, including 2.4M internally displaced persons (IDPs). Following the failure of the Gu and Deyr rainy seasons, the Somali government declared a drought emergency on 10 November 2025, calling for urgent life-saving assistance. Bay Region, particularly Baydhaba district, has been among the most severely affected areas, hosting the highest number of people in need of WASH assistance, with 406,711 people in need identified (HNRP 2025). Despite the needs, only 20.6% of WASH requirements under the HNRP 2025 are currently funded, leaving critical gaps in life-saving services.ltbrgtIn this context, this six-month intervention aims to provide life-saving assistance and inclusive access to safe water for drought-affected and hard-to-reach rural communities in three villages in Baydhaba district. The intervention will ensure immediate access to safe drinking water (Output 1), support the construction and rehabilitation of sustainable water infrastructures (Output 2), and strengthen community capacities for long-term management and water quality assurance (Output 3). A total of 15,000 individuals (2,500 households - HHs) will benefit, including 3,900 women, 3,450 men, 3,900 boys, and 3,750 girls. In close coordination with local authorities, ABC partners, and the WASH Cluster, Acted pre-selected Salbuy, Ashagow and Awdiinle villages based on severity of needs and gaps in assistance. ltbrgtFirstly, Acted will deliver emergency drinking water through time-bound water trucking in Salbuy village, where communities have no access to water (A 1.1.2). This life-saving assistance will address immediate needs while rehabilitation of the local water system is underway (A 1.2.2). The 500 most vulnerable HHs will be selected using the Vulnerability-Based Targeting approach through the SRF tool. Prior to distribution, Village Relief Committees will be established, ensuring the participation of women and vulnerable groups (A 1.1.1). Members will be trained to oversee fair and safe water distribution, support beneficiary selection, mobilize communities, and strengthen accountability throughout the intervention.ltbrgtSecondly, to ensure sustainable access to sufficient, and safe drinking water, Acted will rehabilitate two water points (A 1.2.2) and construct one new borehole (A 1.2.4). Works will include the installation of pumping systems, solar power systems, pipelines, water storage tanks, and accessible water kiosks. Prior to the works, a comprehensive inclusivity assessment will be conducted (A 1.2.1) and a hydrogeological and geophysical study will be conducted prior to drilling a new borehole in Awdiinle (A 1.2.3). Environmental and social risks will be assessed, and mitigation measures integrated into implementation. Construction and rehabilitation works will be carried out by contractors selected through bidding process, with Acted’s technical team overseeing design, quality assurance, and standard compliance. Post-construction monitoring will ensure infrastructures meet community needs.ltbrgtFinally, to promote sustainability, Acted will strengthen community-based water management systems. Water Management Committees will be established or revitalized and trained in operation and maintenance, water quality monitoring, and cost-recovery mechanisms (A 1.3.1). Operational toolkits will be provided to support day-to-day management (A 1.3.2). Particular attention will be given to inclusive representation, ensuring participation of women, minorities, and other vulnerable groups.ltbrgtThe project is designed following the Sphere standards, cluster guidelines, ensuring the inclusion of the most vulnerable groups. Providing immediate life-saving and sustainable solutions will greatly contribute to reducing morbidity and mortality rates. Coordination with WASH clusters, local authorities, communities, and SHF partners will be ensured.ltbrgtlt/pgt
